I went to Florida once back in '98, took the kids to Disney World. Man, the lines were just incredible. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, yeah, I guess so. Even when I’m trying to relax, like when I go fishing with my wife. You'd think fishing would be relaxing, right? But I catch myself tapping my foot on the boat, or talking too loud, or just messing with my tackle box constantly. I can't just sit there and watch the bobber. My wife loves it, though. She grew up on a lake up in Michigan. Her dad had this little aluminum rowboat, real old thing, probably from the fifties. They used to go out at dawn to catch crappie. 

I've never been a morning person myself. Working the late shifts cleaning the building, you get used to being up when everyone else is asleep. The building is so quiet at 2 AM. Sometimes the only sound is the hum of the vending machines in the breakroom. They put in one of those new machines that takes credit cards, but it's always breaking down. Last week, it ate a guy's dollar and he got so mad he kicked the glass. Didn't break it, but left a big scuff mark I had to buff out. Buffing those floors is an art, really. You gotta use the right pad on the machine, or you'll strip the finish right off. 

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, doing things I enjoy. Yeah, even at bingo night. I'm tapping my pencil, shifting around... it gets hard for me to just be quiet and enjoy it.

Well, it really feels like that restlessness, you know? It's just this constant need to be doing something. Like, on my shifts, I'll go straight from mopping the lobby to checking the trash cans, and then I'm off straightening the chairs in the conference rooms without even taking a breath or stopping. I've got this huge pegboard out there for all my tools. I spent a whole weekend outlining every single wrench and hammer with a black marker so I'd know exactly where they go. My neighbor, Dave, saw me doing it and thought I was crazy. He keeps all his tools thrown into this one rusty metal toolbox he got at a garage sale. I don't know how he ever finds anything in there. It's always the 10-millimeter, isn't it? I swear those things just vanish into thin air. I had to go to the hardware store just to buy a replacement, and they sell them individually now just because people lose them so much. The guy at the hardware store, Frank, he's been working there since I was in high school. He knows where every single screw and bolt is in that place. 

But, uh... what were you asking? Oh, right, the restlessness. Yeah, it's definitely that internal feeling. I just can't seem to stop moving, whether I'm at work or at home.

I honestly couldn't tell you. I've never really paid attention to whether my mind wanders more or less when I actually like what I'm doing. 

Like, I really enjoy watching those history documentaries on PBS. The ones about big engineering projects? They had this one on the Hoover Dam a few weeks ago. Fascinating stuff. Did you know they had to run hundreds of miles of pipes through the concrete and pump ice water through them just to cool it down? The narrator said otherwise it would have taken a hundred years for the concrete to cure. A hundred years! I actually went out to see it back in '98. Me and the wife took a trip to Vegas for our anniversary. We didn't gamble much, though. The casinos are just too loud, all those bells and flashing lights, and the cigarette smoke gets right in your eyes. But the buffets, oh man. We went to this one at the Excalibur, and they had a carving station with prime rib that was just out of this world. She was so proud, she actually wanted to get it mounted, but I told her taxidermy prices have gone through the roof. My buddy Jim had a buck mounted last fall and it cost him an arm and a leg, plus the guy took six months to finish it. He had his shop over on Route 9, but I think they're tearing that whole strip mall down to build condos. Everything's condos these days, you know? There's no open space left. \n\nBut, uh... yeah, so even doing that stuff, fishing or bingo, I just get so fidgety. It gets really hard for me to just be quiet and actually enjoy the downtime like she does.\n\nDoctor: Do you often have mood swings?\n\nPatient: Mood swings? No, I don't think so. I mean, I get a little grumpy if I skip lunch, but who doesn't, right? Like last Tuesday, I didn't get to eat because the main cafeteria at the building was totally shut down for an emergency clean. A water pipe burst right over the prep stations. What an absolute mess. The emergency plumbers they called in must have charged a fortune for a rush job like that. \n\nI used to know a plumber, Gary, who would've fixed it for half the price. He drove this beat-up old Ford Econoline van that was always breaking down on him. We spent an entire Saturday once just trying to swap out the alternator in his driveway. His wife brought us out some iced tea while we were working, and man, it was the best sweet tea I’ve ever had. She was from somewhere down South, Georgia maybe? They put peaches in everything down there. I love a good peach cobbler. My grandma used to make one every Fourth of July, and we'd eat it out on the porch watching the fireworks over the lake. They don't do the lake fireworks anymore, though, because of the fire hazard with the dry brush. \n\nBut, uh... wait, what was the question? Oh, mood swings. Yeah, no, I'm pretty even-keeled. Just a regular guy. Nothing like that.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?\n\nPatient: Talk more than others? I guess maybe sometimes, but mostly I just like a good conversation. You know, you get to talking with folks and one thing leads to another. Like the other day, I was down in the basement of the building, just emptying out the recycling bins, and the new security guard, Marcus, was down there. Nice kid, just out of the military. He was telling me about this deployment he had in Germany, and it got me thinking about my uncle who was stationed there back in the seventies. \n\nMy uncle brought back this amazing cuckoo clock from the Black Forest. Real intricate wood carving, little dancers that came out on the hour. He gave it to my mom, and she kept it in the hallway for years. The ticking used to drive my dad absolutely crazy, though. He was a light sleeper. He worked the night shift at the bottling plant, so he had to sleep during the day. That plant closed down, what, fifteen years ago now? They turned the whole lot into one of those fancy outdoor shopping centers. The ones with the brick walkways and the overpriced coffee shops. I went in there once to get a cappuccino and it cost me seven bucks. Seven bucks for a cup of coffee! And the cup wasn't even that big. \n\nBut, uh, talking too much... Oh, right, the sitting still. Yeah, it's like a motor running inside me. I just can't stay put during those meetings.\n\nDoctor: Do you think you would have trouble sitting still even if you were doing something you really enjoyed?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, I guess so. Even when I’m trying to relax, like when I go fishing with my wife. You'd think fishing would be relaxing, right? They used to go out at dawn to catch crappie. \n\nI've never been a morning person myself. Working the late shifts cleaning the building, you get used to being up when everyone else is asleep. He was a light sleeper. He worked the night shift at the bottling plant, so he had to sleep during the day. That plant closed down, what, fifteen years ago now? They turned the whole lot into one of those fancy outdoor shopping centers. The ones with the brick walkways and the overpriced coffee shops. I went in there once to get a cappuccino and it cost me seven bucks. Seven bucks for a cup of coffee! And the cup wasn't even that big. \n\nBut, uh, talking too much... I don't know if I talk more than anyone else. I just have a lot of stories, I guess. People seem to listen, mostly. Or they nod, anyway.\n\nDoctor: Are your difficulties with sitting still and fidgeting causing problems for you at home or with your family?\n\nPatient: Well, at home my wife mostly just rolls her eyes, but it's actually at work where it's turning into a real headache. I've been getting a lot of complaints lately, and my supervisor is constantly correcting me. He says I'm always missing parts of his instructions, and apparently, I'm creating a lot of friction during the room turnovers and when we have to make supply decisions. It got to the point where he actually pushed me toward the employee assistance program. \n\nSpeaking of supply decisions, you wouldn't believe the new floor wax corporate is making us use. I went to Florida once back in '98, took the kids to Disney World. Man, the lines were just incredible. We waited two hours just to get on Space Mountain, and then the ride broke down right when we got to the very front! My youngest started crying, and he dropped his Mickey Mouse ice cream bar right on the hot pavement. Those ice cream bars were a total rip-off, too. I think they were like five bucks back then, I can't even imagine what they charge now.\n\nBut, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if it's causing problems. Yeah, so my supervisor wants me doing this EAP thing because of the friction with the turnovers and all that.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your main problem is that you can't sit still or that you have trouble focusing on what's going on around you?\n\nPatient: Well, I think it's the sitting still part. Well, it's definitely from the inside. It's not like a bird flies by the window and I have to get up. It's more like... I feel like I've got this motor humming right under my skin, you know? Especially when I'm supposed to just sit there, like during those staff meetings at work or the briefings we have before church events. I just can't take it. That storage lot used to be a drive-in theater when I was a kid. We used to sneak in by hiding in the trunk of my buddy Dave's Chevy Nova. Dave was a wild one, he actually joined the Navy and ended up stationed in... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely an inside restless feeling, like a motor that just won't shut off.
